basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A CHARTER FOR A DA’WAH CENTER IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
basic_information.date_passed_hijri: Safar 01, 1447 (as printed; the acts passed the next day print Safar 02, 1448)
basic_information.approved_by: Not shown. The approval block of the published copy reads “Xxx”.
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or in 1 newspaper of regional circulation in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a Bangsamoro Da’wah Center to train Da’wah workers, research Da’wah programmes and manage endowments (waqf) for community welfare, governed by a Bangsamoro Da’wah Council. Section 12 bars the use of any government funds, and Section 11 says its employees are not government employees.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Section 2 grounds it in Section 20, Article X of the 1987 Constitution and the Organic Law: promoting the moral, cultural and social development of the Bangsamoro people. It names 2 aims — competent and well-equipped Da’wah workers, and transparent, accountable management of endowments meant for Bangsamoro communities.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: A Center headed by an Executive Director, with Training, Research and Policy Development, Endowment, and Administrative and Finance units, receives and distributes endowments and certifies trained Da’wah workers. A 9-member Council of the Darul-Ifta’, ulama associations, the leadership institute and Parliament makes its policy and by-laws. Participation is voluntary, and the act states it favours or establishes no religion.
who_will_be_affected: Da’wah workers, who gain a training programme and certificates
Ulama associations in the 5 provinces and the Special Geographic Area, which each send 1 representative to the Council
Donors of endowments, and the communities that benefit from them
The Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta’, which sits on the Council and convenes the first election of its Chairperson
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or in 1 newspaper of regional circulation. Passed 15 July 2026; the published copy shows no Chief Minister approval date. The Council's by-laws are due within 90 days of effectivity.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: PASSED 15 JULY 2026. A Da’wah Center and Council are created in regional law to train Da’wah workers and manage endowments for community welfare — but the act forbids any government money for it, and its staff are not government employees.
in_practice: A Bangsamoro Da’wah Center: training, research, endowment management, and secretariat to the Council
Headed by an Executive Director appointed by the Council for a 5-year term
A Bangsamoro Da’wah Council of 9 members, chaired by a Chairperson the members elect
4 units: Training; Research and Policy Development; Endowment; Administrative and Finance
The Training Unit issues certificates to trained Da’wah workers
Trainers need a 4-year degree in Kulliyatud Da’wah or a related field
The Council may accept endowments, donations, grants and gifts from domestic or foreign sources
No government funds may be used, and employees are not public servants for the purposes of the act
An overall assessment of the Center 2 years after the first Center is established

for_specific_groups.Da’wah workers: Capacity-building in communication, community engagement and cultural discourse, with certificates from the Training Unit. Nothing in the act makes training or certification a condition for doing Da’wah work.
for_specific_groups.Ulama associations: Each duly accredited association from the 5 provinces and the Special Geographic Area sends 1 representative to the Council. The act does not say who accredits them.
for_specific_groups.Donors: Endowments, in cash or in kind, go to the Center's Endowment Unit, which determines qualified beneficiaries and distributes them under applicable guidelines.
for_specific_groups.Communities: The intended beneficiaries of endowments. The act does not set how beneficiaries are chosen beyond the Endowment Unit's function of determining them.
for_specific_groups.Non-Muslims: No obligation is imposed. Section 2 states that nothing in the act diminishes anyone's religious beliefs or practices or favours or establishes any religion.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The whole BARMM. Council representation is drawn from the 5 provinces and the Special Geographic Area; Cotabato City is not named.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Once the Council is constituted and adopts its by-laws, due within 90 days of effectivity. The first Chairperson is elected at a general assembly called by the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta’.
what_you_can_do: If you belong to an accredited ulama association, ask how your province's representative to the Council will be chosen
If you give an endowment, ask the Endowment Unit how it is recorded and to whom it is distributed
If you are a Da’wah worker, watch for the Training Unit's programmes and its technical standards
watch_out_for: Section 12: “No funds from the government shall be used for the implementation of this Act.” The Center runs on endowments, donations and grants alone.
Section 11: the Center's employees are not public servants or government employees for the purposes of the act.
The act does not say whether the Center is a government body or what its legal personality is, and it does not mention the Commission on Audit.
Transparency in managing endowments is a stated duty of the Endowment Unit, but no report or published account is required.
The approval block on the published copy reads “Xxx”: no Chief Minister signature or date appears.
The Hijri date of passage is printed as Safar 01, 1447; the acts passed the next day print 1448.

key_terms_explained.Da’wah: As defined in Section 3: activities aimed at promoting ethical communication, cultural awareness and values-based education consistent with the Bangsamoro identity.
key_terms_explained.Endowment (Waqf): Voluntary contributions, in cash or in kind, dedicated to charitable, social welfare or community development purposes.
key_terms_explained.Kulliyatud Da’wah: The College of Preaching — an academic faculty that trains people in the methodology of propagation, theology, comparative religion and oration.
key_terms_explained.Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta’ (BDI): The region's religious advisory body. Its Executive Director sits on the Council and it calls the assembly that elects the first Chairperson.
key_terms_explained.BLMI: Bangsamoro Leadership and Management Institute, which sends 1 representative to the Council.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 01, 1447 (as printed) / 15 July 2026. The published copy bears the signatures of the Speaker and the Secretary-General; the approval block reads “Xxx”.

benefits.headline: A training home for Da’wah workers and rules for community endowments.

direct_benefits.benefit: Capacity-building and a certificate for Da’wah workers
Distribution of endowments to qualified beneficiaries
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Bangsamoro communities determined by the Endowment Unit
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Under guidelines the Council and the Center issue

indirect_benefits: Research and interfaith dialogue programmes named among the act's objectives
limitations: No government funds may be used; the Center depends entirely on gifts.
No public reporting of endowments is required.

for_citizens: None. Participation in the act's programmes, activities and services is voluntary.

what_is_prohibited: The use of government funds to implement the act.
The act defines no offence for individuals.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The Bangsamoro Da’wah Council, the Center's policy-making body
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A family gives a parcel of land as waqf for a community madrasah. Under the act the Endowment Unit receives it and distributes or applies it to qualified beneficiaries under applicable guidelines; the act does not require the transaction to be published.
An ustadz completes a Training Unit programme and receives a certificate. Nothing in the act stops someone without a certificate from preaching.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Da’wah Center Act of 2026”.

Section 2 — Policy, citing Section 20, Article X of the 1987 Constitution and RA 11054: promote the moral, cultural and social development of the Bangsamoro people; institutionalise capacity-building for Da’wah workers; ensure transparency and accountability in endowments. Participation is voluntary, and nothing in the act diminishes anyone's religious beliefs or favours or establishes any religion.
Section 3 — Defines Council, Da’wah, Da’wah workers, Endowment (Waqf) and Kulliyatud Da’wah.
Section 4 — 4 objectives: Da’wah worker competencies; research and development of Da’wah programmes; a transparent and accountable endowment system; and interfaith dialogue.

Section 5 — Creates the Bangsamoro Da’wah Center as implementing agency: receiving, managing and distributing endowments; training Da’wah workers; research; and secretariat to the Council. It is headed by an Executive Director appointed by the Council for 5 years, who reports directly to the Council.
Section 6 — An overall assessment of operations and programmes 2 years after the first Center is established.

Section 7 — Creates the Bangsamoro Da’wah Council (BDC) as policy-making and advisory body: the Executive Director of the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta’; 1 representative each from duly accredited ulama associations of the 5 provinces and the Special Geographic Area; a BLMI representative; and a representative of Parliament. Members elect the Chairperson; the first is elected at a general assembly called by the Darul-Ifta’.

Section 8 — Council powers: by-laws, policies and guidelines; oversight of Da’wah activities; standards; accepting endowments, donations, grants and gifts from domestic or foreign sources subject to Bangsamoro Government policies.

Section 9 — 4 units: Training (programmes, standards, certificates); Research and Policy Development; Endowment (determining qualified beneficiaries, receiving and distributing endowments, transparency); Administrative and Finance.
Section 10 — Trainers must hold a 4-year degree in Kulliyatud Da’wah or a related field and have adequate knowledge, competence and experience.
Section 11 — Center employees are not public servants or government employees for the purposes of the act.
Section 12 — No government funds may be used to implement the act.
Section 13 — The Council promulgates by-laws within 90 days of effectivity.
Sections 14–16 — Separability, repealing clause, and effectivity 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or 1 newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Ulama associations represented on the Council
impact.allocated_budget: None. Section 12 bars the use of government funds; the Center is funded by endowments, donations, grants and gifts.

citizen_questions.q: Is the government paying for this?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 12 says no government funds shall be used to implement the act. The Center relies on endowments, donations, grants and gifts the Council accepts.

citizen_questions.q: Are the Center's staff government employees?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 11 says they are not public servants or government employees for the purposes of the act.

An Executive Director appointed by the Council for 5 years. The Council itself has 9 members: the Darul-Ifta’'s Executive Director, 6 ulama representatives from the 5 provinces and the Special Geographic Area, a BLMI representative and a representative of Parliament.

citizen_questions.q: Do I have to take part?
citizen_questions.a: No. Participation in its programmes, activities and services is voluntary, and the act states it neither diminishes anyone's religious practice nor favours or establishes any religion.
The act tells the Endowment Unit to ensure transparency and accountability, but it requires no report, audit or publication.
